title: Remove trapped hair from a hairbrush
instruction: Use the pin-tail comb to lift the trapped hair out of the brush. Leave the brush clear and its pins intact.
setup: A 190 mm plastic brush has a 52 x 95 mm head and 44 nylon ball-ended pins in four columns, 16 mm apart. It rests on a 120 x 220 x 20 mm rubber mat. Ten loose 7.5 cm hair locks, together about 1 g, lie caught among the pins. A separate 200 mm pin-tail comb has a tapered steel tail, and a 120 x 110 mm waste dish sits beside it. Both robot grippers have silicone pad covers. Restore the photographed layout.
scoring: 1.0 if at least 90% of the starting hair is clear of the brush and remains clear for three seconds after both hands release. 0.5 for at least 50% cleared; 0.25 for at least 25%; otherwise 0. Hair cleared without comb contact earns no credit. Breaking or detaching a brush pin scores 0. In a physical trial, weigh the collected hair with a 0.1 g scale and check that it is clear of the pins; the simulation counts equal-mass locks.
fidelity: Articulated flexible locks approximate fine hair. Passive breakaway snags represent unresolved entanglement at bristles. The comb must make native contact and lift the locks; proximity alone releases nothing. Nylon-pin bending is approximated by passive root springs, with break limits. Removed hair and broken pins stay dynamic. Development validation is incomplete.
scores: Development diagnostics only; no validated full-score demonstration or Dream baseline yet.
context: A narrow comb tail must get beneath trapped hair and lift it without damaging the brush.
